definitions.gloss: stationing; being posted; residing for duty
definitions.explanation: Being assigned to live and work at a particular location, especially overseas, for work purposes. Commonly used for diplomats, company employees on overseas assignments, and police officers assigned to local posts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{三年間|さんねんかん}→三年間：28861_sannenkan⟧⟦アメリカ→アメリカ：01769_amerika⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{駐在|ちゅうざい}⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: My father was posted in America for three years.

examples.japanese: {駐在|ちゅうざい}さん⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧{通学路|つうがくろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}っている→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: The local police officer stands along the school route every morning.
examples.notes: 駐在さん is a colloquial way to refer to a resident police officer.

examples.japanese: ⟦{来月|らいげつ}→来月：00744_raigetsu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧シンガポール⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{駐在|ちゅうざい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧こと⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なり→なる：01970_naru⟧、⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す→引っ越す：01171_hikkosu⟧⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I'll be posted to Singapore starting next month, so we're preparing for the family to move.

notes:
USAGE:
Very common in business contexts for overseas assignments. A {駐在員|ちゅうざいいん} (expatriate employee) is someone posted abroad by their company. In rural Japan, {駐在|ちゅうざい}さん refers to the local resident police officer stationed at a small police box (⟦{駐在所|ちゅうざいしょ}→駐在所：19187_chuuzaisho⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {駐在員|ちゅうざいいん} (expatriate employee; stationed worker)
- ⟦{駐在所|ちゅうざいしょ}→駐在所：19187_chuuzaisho⟧ (residential police box)
- {海外|かいがい}{駐在|ちゅうざい} (overseas posting)
- {駐在|ちゅうざい}{妻|づま} (expat wife)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{赴任|ふにん}→赴任：10601_funin⟧: taking up a post — focuses on the act of going to a new assignment
- ⟦{常駐|じょうちゅう}→常駐：21124_jouchuu⟧: permanent stationing — being stationed full-time at a client site or location
